objective: Determine whether a general polynomial decision test for safe splitting on two-use guarded schedules would decide strict 3-SAT, even for a single crossing middle and fixed wiring per source width.
status: Proved: Recognizing a safe split of one middle is NP-hard on two-use schedules fixed per source width, both for all observed triples and for the outer pair after the cut bit is hidden. General triple equality in this one-middle setting can be tested with four nonadaptive SAT queries.
title: The cost of recognizing when equality can be dropped on unrestricted blocks
